audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7702 authorization nonce properly validated to prevent same-chain replay attacks?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Nonce validation exists in IsValidForExecution method. Line 316-321 compares authorizationTuple.Nonce against WorldState.GetNonce(authorizationTuple.Authority). The check requires exact match (authNonce != authorizationTuple.Nonce).
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Nonce validation occurs before delegation is applied. Line 316-321 explicitly rejects mismatched nonces with descriptive error message.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Proper nonce validation implemented. Replay protection enforced via exact nonce match requirement.

audit_items.title: Can type alias constructors (Address, Root, VersionedHash, Bloom) be bypassed to create instances with incorrect byte lengths?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Nethermind uses strongly-typed wrappers. Address is 20 bytes fixed. Deserialization paths (RLP/SSZ) perform length validation.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Type constructors enforce length constraints. RLP decoder validates lengths during deserialization.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - C# type system and RLP validation provide defense-in-depth.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-022: Can an attacker forge a transaction signature that recovers to a different sender address?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: ECDSA signature recovery uses SpanSecP256k1.RecoverKeyFromCompact. MaxLowS constant defined for s-value validation. Signature malleability prevented by s <= HalfN check in TxValidator.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Secp256k1 library handles curve operations. BaseSignatureTxValidator enforces s < HalfNPlusOne (EIP-2 low-s requirement).
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Standard ECDSA recovery with proper s-value bounds checking.

audit_items.title: Verify Execution Client Transaction Authentication: Does the execution client properly validate recovered sender addresses?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Sender recovery performed independently in EthereumEcdsaExtensions.RecoverAddress. Transaction validation includes signature validation before execution.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Signature validation occurs during tx validation. No TOCTOU as recovered address is used consistently.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Proper sender authentication with consistent recovered address usage.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006/tb-001: Is ECDSA signature verification correctly enforced for all EIP-7702 Authorization tuples?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: EIP-7702 authorization signature recovery in line 251 via Ecdsa.RecoverAddress(authTuple). Signature validation checks s-value bounds at lines 300-305.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Signature recovery uses correct message hash (Eip7702Constants.Magic prefix + RLP encoding). s > HalfN check at line 300.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Proper ECDSA verification with malleability protection.

audit_items.title: Verify EIP-7702 Authorizer Authentication: Can an attacker forge authorization to impersonate the actor-eip7702-authorizer?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Authorization recovery constructs proper message hash with Magic byte prefix and RLP-encoded tuple data. Recovery uses standard ECDSA.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - No bypass path identified. All authorization tuples go through RecoverAddress.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Standard cryptographic signature verification.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is the ECDSA signature s-value validated to be in the lower half of secp256k1 curve order?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Line 300-301: 'UInt256 s = new(authorizationTuple.AuthoritySignature.SAsSpan, isBigEndian: true); if (... || s > Secp256K1Curve.HalfN ...)'. Direct check against HalfN constant.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - s > HalfN results in 'Bad signature' error. Secp256K1Curve.HalfN = N/2 correctly defined.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Malleability protection properly implemented.

audit_items.title: Does signature malleability in EIP-7702 Authorization allow recovery to an unintended address?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: HalfN = N/2, HalfNPlusOne = HalfN + 1. s-value check at TransactionProcessor.cs:300 uses s > HalfN (which is stricter than s >= HalfNPlusOne). Malleability prevented.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Malleable signatures (s > HalfN) are rejected before recovery.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Malleable signatures rejected.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does the EIP-7702 authorization validation correctly reject ecrecover results returning address(0)?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Line 299-302 checks 'authorizationTuple.Authority is null' which handles ecrecover returning null (equivalent to address(0)). Failed recovery results in null Authority.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Null authority check precedes all other validation. Bad signature error returned.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Null/zero address recovery properly rejected.

audit_items.title: Is the transaction sender validation robust against address(0) authorization attacks at the P2P boundary?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: RecoverAuthorityFilter runs during tx pool acceptance, recovering authorities before transaction enters mempool. Failed recovery leaves Authority as null.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - TxPool validation pipeline includes authority recovery. DelegatedAccountFilter handles null Authority cases.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - P2P boundary validation includes authority recovery.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the EIP-7702 Authorization chain_id field validated against the current chain ID?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Lines 283-287: 'if (authorizationTuple.ChainId != 0 && SpecProvider.ChainId != authorizationTuple.ChainId)'. Chain ID 0 is wildcard (per EIP-7702), non-zero must match.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Chain ID validation occurs before delegation application. Mismatch results in rejection with descriptive error.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Proper chain ID validation with wildcard support per spec.

audit_summary.skip_reason: This check concerns the signing side (wallet/authorizer software), not the validation side. Nethermind validates received authorizations but doesn't control how external wallets create them.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is EIP-7702 Authorization nonce validation correctly enforced?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Lines 316-321: 'UInt256 authNonce = WorldState.GetNonce(authorizationTuple.Authority); if (authNonce != authorizationTuple.Nonce)'. Exact nonce match required.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Nonce validation before any state changes. MAX_UINT64 check at lines 289-293.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Proper nonce validation with overflow protection.

audit_items.title: Can an attacker replay an EIP-7702 Authorization after the authorizer's nonce has incremented?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: After successful authorization processing, nonce is incremented at line 267: 'WorldState.IncrementNonce(authority)'. Replayed authorization would fail nonce check.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Nonce increment is atomic with delegation application. Replay rejected at validation.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Replay protection via nonce increment.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is the authorizer's nonce incremented after successful EIP-7702 authorization processing?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Line 267: 'WorldState.IncrementNonce(authority)' called for existing accounts. Line 264: 'WorldState.CreateAccount(authority, 0, 1)' creates new account with nonce 1.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Nonce increment occurs atomically within ProcessDelegations. Both new and existing accounts handled.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Proper nonce increment for replay protection.

audit_items.title: Verify EIP-7702 Authorization Replay Protection: Can the same authorization be accepted twice?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: After first authorization, nonce is incremented. Second submission fails at line 318: 'authNonce != authorizationTuple.Nonce'.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Nonce check ensures one-time use. No race condition possible as state changes are atomic within transaction.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Replay protection enforced.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is the resolution of multiple EIP-7702 Authorizations targeting the same authorizer deterministic?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Line 249: 'foreach (AuthorizationTuple authTuple in tx.AuthorizationList)' - sequential processing. Last valid authorization wins per EIP-7702.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - Deterministic iteration order. SetDelegation at line 270 overwrites previous delegation.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Deterministic 'last wins' semantics.

audit_items.title: Does the transaction sender have the ability to craft authorization sequences that produce implementation-specific behavior?

audit_summary.phase1_findings: Sequential processing of authorization list is deterministic. Invalid authorizations are skipped, valid ones are applied. Last valid wins.
audit_summary.phase2_invariant_check: HOLD - No implementation-specific ambiguity identified. Standard list iteration.
audit_summary.phase3_risk_assessment: LOW RISK - Behavior matches EIP-7702 specification.
